title: Chapter XV

teacherSummary.text: The creature finds Paradise Lost, Plutarch's Lives and The Sorrows of Young Werther, and reads Victor's laboratory journal, which describes his creation with disgust. He reveals himself to the blind old De Lacey, who is kind, but Felix, Agatha and Safie return, and Felix strikes him and drives him away.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “Paradise Lost, a volume of Plutarch’s Lives, and the Sorrows of Werther” slowly and put it in my own words: The creature finds three books: Paradise Lost, Plutarch's Lives and The Sorrows of Werther. Next, craft. I notice the list mixes epic poetry, history and a sentimental novel, the education of his heart and mind. The strongest word is “Paradise”: it points to Milton's poem of creation and fall, the story he will read as his own. Then, effect. Why do the books the creature finds matter? My answer: The books the creature finds matter because Paradise Lost teaches him to see himself as an abandoned Adam or a fallen Satan; the books give him language for his pain and his rage.
